pos: noun or participle which takes the aux. verb suru
headline: Tsūyaku is from Sinitic 通譯 (tōngyì).

sources.quote: From Sinitic 通譯 /通译 (tōngyì).

examples.ja: 彼女は通訳として雇われた。
examples.en: She was engaged as an interpreter.

examples.ja: 叔父は僕に通訳をやらせた。
examples.en: My uncle made me serve as interpreter.

pos: nouns which may take the genitive case particle 'no'
headline: Kazan is Middle Chinese 火山, literally “flaming mountain”.

sources.quote: From Middle Chinese 火山 (xwa^X srean, literally “flaming mountain”).

examples.ja: 火山が再び活動を始めた。
examples.en: The volcano has become active again.

examples.ja: 火山は炎と溶岩を吹き出す。
examples.en: The volcano shoots out flames and lava.

headline: Wakare is the continuative stem of 別れる (wakareru, “to separate, to part ways, to bid farewell”).

sources.quote: The 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 別(わか)れる (wakareru, “to separate, to part ways, to bid farewell, to break up”).

examples.en: To meet is to part.
We never meet without a parting.

headline: Bu, “non-”, is from Middle Chinese 無, the kan'on reading, so likely a later borrowing.

sources.quote: From Middle Chinese 無 (bu). The 漢音 (kan'on), so likely a later borrowing.

headline: Ku, “phrase”, is from Middle Chinese 句 (kjuᴴ, “phrase”).

sources.quote: From Middle Chinese 句 (kjuᴴ, “phrase”).

examples.ja: この句はどう意味ですか。
examples.en: What is the meaning of this phrase?

examples.ja: 辞書でその句を調べなさい。
examples.en: Look up the phrase in your dictionary.

meaning: to attack (an enemy), to beat, to finish off
headline: Yattsukeru is a shift from 遣り付ける (yaritsukeru): yari plus 付ける (tsukeru, “perform an action vigorously”).

sources.quote: Shift from 遣(や)り付(つ)ける (yaritsukeru), itself a compound of やり (yari, the 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb やる (yaru, “to dispatch; to do”)) + 付(つ)ける (tsukeru, “perform an action vigorously”).

headline: Shina is simply from Old Japanese.

sources.quote: From Old Japanese.

examples.ja: ここでお買い上げの品は無料で配達します。
examples.en: Articles bought here will be delivered free of charge.

headline: Jōhō is a contraction of 情況報告 (jōkyō hōkoku, “situation report”).

sources.quote: Contraction of 情(じょう)況(きょう)報(ほう)告(こく) (jōkyō hōkoku, “situation report”).

examples.en: His information is certain.
This information is confidential.

headline: Kochira is こち (kochi, “this direction (or person)”) plus 等 (-ra, suffix of rough indication or approximation).

morphemes.meaning: suffix of rough indication or approximation

sources.quote: From こち (kochi, “this direction (or person)”) + 等(ら) (-ra, suffix of rough indication or approximation).

headline: Tēpurekōdā is borrowed from English tape recorder.

sources.quote: Borrowed from English tape recorder.

examples.ja: テープレコーダーは有用な教具です。
examples.en: The tape recorder is a useful aid to teaching.

examples.ja: これは君のテープレコーダーですか。
examples.en: Is this your tape recorder?

pos: noun or participle which takes the aux. verb suru
headline: Tsūkin was coined after 通う (kayou, “to regularly visit”) and 勤め (tsutome), with the kanji shifted to on'yomi in the compound.

sources.quote: Coined after 通(かよ)う (kayou, “to regularly visit”) and 勤(つと)め (tsutome) or 勤務(きんむ) (kinmu, “job, occupation”). Kanji shifted to on'yomi in the compound.

examples.en: I commute to work for an hour.

examples.ja: 彼はバスで通勤している。
examples.en: He commutes to his office by bus.

headline: Tsukue, “desk”, is simply listed as inherited from Old Japanese.

sources.quote: Inherited from Old Japanese.

pos: nouns which may take the genitive case particle 'no'
headline: Reigai is 例 (rei, “usual practice”) plus 外 (gai, “outside”): outside the usual practice.

sources.quote: 例(れい) (rei, “usual practice”) + 外(がい) (gai, “outside”)

examples.ja: 例外は原則のある証拠。
examples.en: The exception proves the rule.

examples.ja: 例外のないルールはない。
examples.en: There is no rule without exceptions.

meaning: well (used when making a modest or hesitant statement)
headline: Mā is onomatopoeic.

sources.quote: Onomatopoeic.

examples.en: Oh no, really?
Well, you can't.

headline: Omowazu is the negative continuative of 思う.

sources.quote: From the negative continuative of 思う.

examples.en: He laughed in spite of himself.
I wept in spite of myself.

headline: Zenzen is an orthographic borrowing from Chinese 全然 (quánrán) in the early 1800s, at first with furigana reading it まったく (mattaku).

sources.quote: Orthographic borrowing from Chinese 全然 (quánrán) in the early 1800s from 白(はく)話(わ)小(しょう)説(せつ) (hakuwa shōsetsu, literally “vernacular novels”), a genre using more colloquial styles, initially with furigana indicating a reading of まったく (mattaku, “completely”).
First cited to a text from 1823, with the ぜんぜん (zenzen) reading becoming more common starting from the late 1890s.

examples.en: I have no plans whatever.
I have no idea.

headline: Chōmiryō is 調味 (chōmi, “seasoning”) plus 料 (-ryō, “material”).

sources.quote: 調味(ちょうみ) (chōmi, “seasoning”) + 料(りょう) (-ryō, “material”)

meaning: to attach, to join, to add
headline: Tsukeru is from Old Japanese 付く (tuku), following the lower bigrade conjugation.

sources.quote: From Old Japanese 付く (tuku), following 下二段活用 (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”).
Development

Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 下(しも)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “lower monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -eru.
First attested in the Nihon Shoki of 720 CE.

examples.en: Get to work, everybody.
He turned on the radio.

pos: nouns which may take the genitive case particle 'no'
headline: Gendai is 現 (gen, “current, now”) plus 代 (dai, “age, period”).

sources.quote: From 現(げん) (gen, “current, now”) + 代(だい) (dai, “age, period”)

examples.en: He's the Bach of today.

examples.ja: 彼は現代音楽が好きだ。
examples.en: He has a liking for modern music.

meaning: to plunge into, to stick into
headline: Tsukkomu is 突く (tsuku, “to poke”) plus 込む (komu, “to put into”).

sources.quote: 突(つ)く (tsuku, “to poke”) + 込(こ)む (komu, “to put into”)

examples.en: The car ran into a tree.

examples.ja: 彼は本を鞄につっこんだ。
examples.en: He stuck the book in his bag.

headline: Hyōhon is Literary Chinese 標本 (biāoběn), “the uppermost branches and the root”.

sources.quote: Literary Chinese 標本 (biāoběn, “the uppermost branches and the root”)

examples.ja: たとえば、標本はいくつですか。
examples.en: How many samples, for example?

examples.ja: これらの標本はいくつかの種類に分類される。
examples.en: These specimens are divided into several categories.

pos: nouns which may take the genitive case particle 'no'
headline: Murasaki is possibly 群 (mura, “gathering, group”) plus 咲き (saki, “blooming”).

sources.quote: From Old Japanese.
Possibly a compound of 群 (mura, “gathering, group”) + 咲き (saki, “blooming”, the 連用形 (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of verb 咲く (saku), “to bloom”).

examples.ja: 赤と青を混ぜると紫になる。
examples.en: Red and blue paint mixed together give us purple.

examples.ja: その色はピンクというより紫だ。
examples.en: The color is purple rather than pink.

headline: Jun, “order”, is from Middle Chinese 順 (MC zywinH).

sources.quote: From Middle Chinese 順 (MC zywinH).

headline: Nasaru is 成す (nasu, “to do”) plus a classical る suffix, irregularly evolved to godan conjugation.

sources.quote: From 成(な)す (nasu, “to do”) + classical る (-ru, passive/honorific/potential suffix) (modern れる (-reru)). Irregularly evolved to godan conjugation.

headline: Kawaku, “to be thirsty”, is related to 乾く (kawaku, “dry”).

sources.quote: Related to 乾(かわ)く (kawaku, “dry”).

examples.ja: お腹が空いたし、のども渇いた。
examples.en: I'm hungry and thirsty.

headline: Kushi, “comb”, is cognate with 串 (kushi, “skewer”).

sources.quote: Cognate with 串 (kushi, “skewer”).

examples.en: This is a wooden comb.

examples.ja: 私は木のくしを持っています。
examples.en: I have a wooden comb.

headline: Kaisūken is 回数 (kaisū, “number of times”) plus 券 (ken, “ticket”).

sources.quote: Compound of 回(かい)数(すう) (kaisū, “number of times”) + 券(けん) (ken, “ticket”).

examples.en: May I have coupon tickets?

pos: nouns which may take the genitive case particle 'no'
headline: Kaigai is Middle Chinese 海外, literally “sea + outside, beyond”.

sources.quote: From Middle Chinese 海外 (MC xojX ngwajH, literally “sea + outside, beyond”). Compare modern Mandarin 海外 (hǎiwài).

examples.en: He goes abroad every year.
He studied abroad.

headline: Hara is often compared to Korean 배 (bae, “stomach”), but Vovin rejects this.

sources.quote: Often compared to Korean 배 (bae, “stomach”), but Vovin rejects this.

examples.en: The belly is not filled with fair words.
You can't make an omelet without breaking eggs.

headline: Koishii is inherited from Old Japanese 恋し (koishi).

sources.quote: Inherited from Old Japanese 恋し (koishi).

examples.en: He longed for his mother.

examples.ja: あなたがとても恋しい。
examples.en: I miss you so much.
